The project uses Zod 4 (zod ^4). Its `looseObject` is used for forward compatibility, so records and project.yaml are loose objects at every level [dec-094vmt9t].

The published JSON Schema comes from Zod 4's built-in `toJSONSchema`, which removes the need for a separate dependency [dec-094vmt9t]. To regenerate it, run `pnpm --filter @aimem/schema build`. That refreshes `dist/record.schema.json` and `project.schema.json`. Then review the snapshot diff and update the snapshot deliberately [run-17vbsk09].

A snapshot test (`json-schema.test.ts`) guards the exported schema contract, and it was passing on 2026-10-11 [tst-cw10hn77][dec-094vmt9t].

Claims use compare-and-swap on a dedicated branch. Live claims are stored as JSON on a separate `aimem-live` branch. To acquire a claim, you fetch, check the current holder, commit and push. If the push is rejected, you retry, so two clones cannot both win [dec-kqfc1se7].

Supporting details:
- Each task has one claim file with holder, session, paths, since, heartbeat and ttl. The invariant is at most one live holder per task [sch-3a3jkgmm].
- Claims must never be committed to feature branches [sch-3a3jkgmm].
- Claim holders are kept out of task files, because writing them there caused merge conflicts on every heartbeat [dec-g17nvbca].
- Trade-offs: it needs network access to the remote, and expired claims can be stolen after the TTL [dec-kqfc1se7].
- The claim format may change before M3 ships [sch-3a3jkgmm].

We evaluated isomorphic-git, a pure-JS git library, and rejected it because of feature gaps in credentials, hooks and worktrees [dec-ghsxv3vg]. 

Instead, all git work shells out to the user's installed git binary via execa, so credentials, hooks and config behave as usual. Reimplementing git would also miss LFS, worktrees and credential helpers [dec-ndgz6y7a].

Consequences: git must be installed (true for every target user) [dec-ndgz6y7a], and tests use real temporary repos instead of mocks [dec-ghsxv3vg].

Record ids are random so that parallel branches never collide. Sequential counters collide when two branches add records at the same time [dec-j2t35mx0].

Ids are a type prefix plus 8 random Crockford base32 characters. The id in the frontmatter is authoritative, and the slug may drift [dec-j2t35mx0].

Tradeoffs: ids are not sortable by time, and validation fails on duplicates [dec-j2t35mx0].

Note that the alphabet detail (excluding i, l, o, u, so typos can't produce a valid id) comes from an agent-written, not human-verified record [mem-8ba67vjm].

After upgrading Biome to 2.5, `biome migrate` rewrote `recommended: true` to `preset: none`, which silently disabled all lint rules [mem-rj2t0xj9][inc-242wrkm4]. Lint kept passing because nothing was being checked, so any lint problem could have reached main unnoticed [mem-rj2t0xj9][inc-242wrkm4].

It was noticed in the migrate output and fixed the same session (2026-10-12) by setting the preset back to recommended and probing with an explicit `any` [inc-242wrkm4]. To prevent a repeat, probe lint after any lint config change; lint should warn with noExplicitAny [inc-242wrkm4][mem-rj2t0xj9].

Note: a record with trust="inferred" claims the project uses ESLint and Prettier, but it is unverified and flagged as contradicting biome.json [mem-yd7935cw].

A `content_sha` made up solely of digits, if left unquoted in YAML frontmatter, is parsed as an integer rather than a string. For example, a placeholder sha of zeros became the number 0, which fails the string check on `source.content_sha` and triggers V002 [mem-hrm4q190].

The fix is to quote hashes and ids that could be all digits when writing frontmatter [mem-hrm4q190].

aimem authenticates to Google for ingestion with a service account that can read one shared inbox folder, rather than per-user OAuth [mem-j4yeeebg]. The stated reasons are least privilege and no consent screens for non-developers. Per-user OAuth remains an option [mem-j4yeeebg].

This sits within the broader decision to offer Upload and Google Drive connectors in v1, which turn Google Docs and Sheets into read-only, externally-owned records [dec-8hscg239].

The records don't describe a private, git-excluded note type. What they do say is related but not the same thing:

- Knowledge lives as markdown records in `.aimem/` committed to git, and the server only indexes them [dec-3by2wh28].
- The only things kept outside git are the rebuildable vector cache under `.aimem/.cache` [sch-nygqk0ka] and live state such as claims, which sit on a separate `aimem-live` branch [sch-3a3jkgmm] and are not durable records [dec-g17nvbca].
- Roles only affect ranking and views, not access; anyone with repo access can read everything [dec-2znaykpx].

Token counts are estimated with a chars/4 heuristic: the number of characters divided by four, with a per-model override available [dec-nppkpt6e]. The decision applies this heuristic to all budgets. An optional tokenizer can be installed later [dec-nppkpt6e].

The reason is that exact tokenizers differ per model and add a heavy dependency [dec-nppkpt6e]. The estimate can be off by roughly 10–20%, so per-section limits are given some headroom [dec-nppkpt6e].

The default briefing budget is 4000 tokens unless project.yaml sets briefing.budget_tokens [mem-q9krtm0g].

INDEX.md tidak boleh diedit manual karena file ini selalu dibuat ulang oleh aimem, sehingga perubahan manual akan hilang pada penulisan berikutnya [mem-xx4j8c41]. (Catatan: sumber ini berstatus trust="agent", belum diverifikasi manusia.)

Alasan tambahan dari keputusan terverifikasi:
- File indeks yang dihasilkan selalu konflik saat dua cabang menambah record. Karena itu INDEX.md ditandai `merge=ours` di .gitattributes dan diregenerasi oleh hook atau CI setelah merge, bukan diedit tangan [dec-v868xmvq].
- Konsekuensinya, isi INDEX.md bisa tertinggal sebentar sampai hook atau CI berjalan [dec-v868xmvq].

Jika isinya salah, perbaiki record sumbernya lalu jalankan `aimem index` [mem-xx4j8c41].

Tidak, server sinkronisasi bersifat opsional dan di-host sendiri oleh tim [dec-e4qh00j3]. Tim kecil atau pengguna solo bisa berjalan hanya dengan git. Server menambahkan klaim realtime, indeks bersama, dan aplikasi web [dec-e4qh00j3].

Konsekuensinya, setiap fitur harus punya jalur yang hanya memakai git atau degradasi yang terdokumentasi [dec-e4qh00j3]. Alasannya, mewajibkan server akan menghalangi kasus penggunaan solo dan menambah beban operasional [dec-e4qh00j3].

The project uses Biome for linting and formatting, per the verified records.

- A verified memory describes upgrading Biome to 2.5 and the `biome migrate` command changing the linter config [mem-rj2t0xj9]. It notes that `recommended: true` had been rewritten to `preset: none`, which silently disabled all lint rules, and that the fix is to set it back to recommended [mem-rj2t0xj9].
- A record claiming ESLint and Prettier is inferred (not human-verified). It says it "contradicts biome.json; needs review" [mem-yd7935cw]. I'd treat it as unreliable, and the verified Biome record takes precedence.

The records don't state explicitly that Biome handles formatting too. The verified memory's title refers to a "Formatter config migration," which suggests it does [mem-rj2t0xj9].

Yes, per the current accepted decision: briefings use hybrid retrieval that fuses BM25 with a local multilingual embedding model, and fall back to lexical-only when no model is present [dec-mtbcq7yr].

- The embeddings work is still open. It covers chunking, an embedding provider interface, a vector cache and a lexical fallback [tsk-w4411vwr]. The BM25 index and search task is also open [tsk-7hfeytzh]. So the embedding path may not be fully built yet.
- The model is not yet chosen. The proposed decision is to pin the smallest multilingual candidate that passes the evals [dec-f30g1hx1].
- One record says search is lexical-only BM25 [mem-1x4y6jd8]. It is inferred and unverified, it rests on a superseded ADR, and it is marked as needing review. The accepted decision above overrides it.

It depends on the mode:

- **Solo projects:** yes. Solo mode implies `agent_commits: commit`, so agents commit notebook changes themselves [dec-ek66gxgx].
- **Team projects:** no, by default. The default is `stage`, so agents stage changes and humans commit them along with their code [dec-ek66gxgx].

A `pr` option is also available [dec-ek66gxgx]. The record doesn't say how `pr` behaves.

This policy is mode-dependent logic in core, not a schema default [dec-ek66gxgx].

A new decision with no explicit status starts as **proposed**. [dec-9h7m0yg3] This follows the spec lifecycle (proposed, then accepted or rejected), and the default is set as `DEFAULT_STATUS.decision = proposed`. [dec-9h7m0yg3] Agents must pass `--status accepted` when a human has already agreed. [dec-9h7m0yg3]

Run these steps in order from the workspace (runbook, human-verified) [run-gea7sjyn]:

1. `pnpm install`
2. `pnpm lint`
3. `pnpm typecheck`
4. `pnpm test`

All three of lint, typecheck and test must exit 0 [run-gea7sjyn]. CI runs the same gate on Linux and macOS with Node 22 and 24 [mem-rmqc83gx]. Test failures may show a shrunk counterexample, since the tests include property tests [mem-rmqc83gx].
